name: Philtrum filler / shortening

card.summary: Reshaping the philtrum and cupid's bow with filler or a lip lift to look shorter and more defined; plenty of cosmetic practice, little formal evidence.
card.aka: Philtrum lift; lip lift; cupid's bow filler
card.note: Surgical versions leave scars; filler carries standard filler risks.

quick.overview:
The philtrum is the groove between the nose and upper lip. Some people seek a shorter philtrum or a sharper cupid's bow, using filler along the lip border or a surgical lip lift.

Surgeons report high satisfaction with lip lifts, but no single technique is standard.[3]
quick.mechanism: Filler adds volume at the lip border and philtral columns. A lip lift removes skin below the nose or along the lip border to expose more of the upper lip; a 2014 review found philtrum length decreased with indirect techniques.[3]
quick.risks: Lip lift risks include visible scarring, numbness, asymmetry, lip distortion and speech or smile changes.[3] Filler carries bruising, lumps, allergic reactions and, rarely, vascular complications.[2]

lead: The philtrum is the vertical groove in the middle of the upper lip, running from the base of the nose to the upper edge of the lip [1]. The cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper-lip border, with peaks that line up with the philtral columns [5]. The philtrum's length sets how much skin sits between the nose and the red of the lip, so it shapes the proportions of the lower face; a short philtrum is associated with a youthful mouth, and upper-lip lengthening is described as a sign of aging [3][12].

Philtrum filler and shortening are cosmetic efforts to make this area look shorter, more defined or more lifted. People pursue them in two broad ways: injecting filler (usually hyaluronic acid) along the lip border and philtral columns for definition, or having a surgical lip lift that removes a strip of skin under the nose or along the lip border so more of the red upper lip shows [2][3][6]. People who choose these procedures describe the aim as a shorter-looking philtrum, a fuller upper lip, a sharper cupid's bow, and a more balanced relationship between nose, lip and chin.

Lip lift techniques have been published since the 1980s, including Austin's 1986 report of 83 patients [12], a 202-patient retrospective review that measured significantly shorter philtrum length [13] and an 823-patient series [14]. Wikipedia's lip lift article notes that surgeons report high patient satisfaction but that no single technique has become the standard, and that a 2014 systematic review found philtrum length decreased with indirect lip lifts but not with V-Y augmentation [3]. No trial specific to filler used to shorten the philtrum was identified.

chain: Skin is removed under the nose, or filler is placed along the lip border
The philtrum measures shorter and the upper lip shows more red
Upper lip looks more lifted and the lower third looks more balanced
angle.text: A subnasal lip lift physically shortens the distance from nose to lip, and filler can add definition to the philtral columns and cupid's bow so the area reads as shorter and more sculpted. People who pursue it describe the goal as a more balanced lower face and a more visible upper lip.

infobox: Filler; direct (gull-wing), subnasal (bullhorn) or corner lip lift; V-Y advancement[3]
About 20 minutes in the operating room[3]
Varies by product: roughly 6 months for some hyaluronic acids, longer for others[6]

paras: The philtrum is a feature of therian mammals; in most mammals it channels odorants toward the vomeronasal organ, while in humans it is described as a vestigial medial depression bordered by ridges called philtral columns [1]. It forms where the nasomedial and maxillary processes meet during embryonic development, and incomplete fusion can cause cleft lip [1].

A flattened or smooth philtrum can accompany conditions such as fetal alcohol syndrome and Prader-Willi syndrome, and one study of prepubertal boys with autism spectrum disorders linked a shorter-than-average philtrum to a cluster of facial features [1]. The vermilion border, the sharp line between lip and skin, forms the cupid's bow, and even 1 mm of misalignment when repairing it can be noticeable [4][5][7].

In aesthetic terms, the philtrum is the skin segment between the base of the nose (subnasale) and the top of the red lip. Wikipedia's lip lift article describes a youthful mouth as lozenge-shaped with a pronounced cupid's bow and fullness in both lips, and says lips shrink, lose definition and sag with age [3]. Surgeon Harvey Austin's 1986 paper drew attention to upper-lip lengthening as a seldom-considered sign of aging [12]. Appearance forums put the same idea as measurements, comparing philtrum length with chin height or midface length [8].

Fillers, commonly hyaluronic acid, add volume and definition at the lip. Wikipedia lists collagen (introduced around 1980), hyaluronic acid gels such as Restylane (reported duration about six months) and Juvederm, a patient's own fat, and implants as lip materials, with durations ranging from weeks for collagen to years for some products [6]. Aimed at the philtrum, filler is placed along the vermilion border and the philtral columns to sharpen the cupid's bow and make the area look more defined; it adds volume and does not remove skin, so the measured length of the philtrum does not change [6].

A 2015 narrative technique review of lip filler in the Journal of Cutaneous and Aesthetic Surgery describes the philtrum and cupid's bow anatomically, says loss of vermilion volume and drooping mouth corners are the most frequent complaints, and notes that overfilling male lips can make them look feminine [15]. It describes medium-depth hyaluronic acid products, needle or cannula delivery, and downtime of about two days to two weeks [15]. Wikipedia notes that overfilling can give an exaggerated look and under-injection can leave ridges [6]. The review says nodules can be dissolved with hyaluronidase and gives that enzyme as the response to blanching from a blocked vessel [15].

The direct lift, sometimes called the gull-wing lift, removes skin at or just above the white roll, moving the red lip upward from the peaks of the cupid's bow; it typically takes about 20 minutes in the operating room. The indirect or subnasal 'bullhorn' lift removes an ellipse of skin under the nose and is often paired with a corner lift [3]. Austin's 1986 paper described excising a wavy ellipse of lip skin with the scar hidden under the nose and reported minimal scars and excellent results in 83 patients [12]. Other variants include a thread lift, which Wikipedia says has fallen out of favour because results are short-lived, a 'double duck' lift that leaves the columella uncut, a corner-of-the-mouth or 'smile' lift, and V-Y advancement made from inside the mouth [3].

Most techniques increase the visible amount of red lip, and V-Y augmentation has measured, statistically significant gains in upper red-lip height and surface area [3]. A 2014 systematic review found that philtrum length decreased with indirect lip lifts but not with V-Y advancement [3]. More recent technique papers include Talei's modified upper lip lift, an 823-patient series using deep-plane release and suspension that builds on the subnasal 'bullhorn' lift [14].

Lip lift complications listed include numbness, stiffness, pain, paraesthesia, lip distortion or lengthening, smile deformation, speech changes and visible or hypertrophic scarring, especially at the white roll. Direct-lift-specific risks are asymmetry and under-correction. Swelling usually settles in one to two weeks and tightness can last two to four months, and bed rest of at least a week is described [3].

Filler complications include redness, swelling, bruising, itching, lumps, implant movement, allergic reactions and infection, with rare vascular events [2][6]. Filler is generally not recommended during active cold sores, clotting problems or active skin conditions, and smoking slows healing [6]. Screening for herpes history and for aspirin or vitamin E use is described in the technique review [15].

Surgeons tried paraffin injections in lips around 1900 without success, and liquid silicone was used from the early 1960s before being abandoned about three decades later over health and long-term appearance concerns [6]. Injectable bovine collagen from around 1980 became the benchmark against which later fillers were measured [6]. In the 1980s, because collagen results were not permanent, surgeons developed lifting and augmentation techniques, with early publications by Fanous (1984), Austin (1986) and Greenwald (1987) [3].

Later work added quantitative and population-specific studies. Wikipedia cites Jacono and Quatela (2004) for measured gains with V-Y augmentation and a 2014 systematic review of non-filling lip augmentation techniques [3]. In a 2015 retrospective chart review of 202 Asian patients, central lip lift significantly shortened philtrum length and increased visible upper vermilion; the authors reported that in this group a long philtrum was mostly due to bone retraction after orthognathic or orthodontic procedures rather than aging, and that about half of patients had the lift for physiognomic reasons [13]. Wikipedia notes, without a citation, that improved non-surgical fillers have reduced demand for lip lifts [3].

A short philtrum is discussed in appearance communities as a youthful and balanced feature, and forum users often describe philtrum length relative to chin height or midface length. Posters share before-and-after photographs, scar-concealment tips and reports from clinics abroad; lip lifts are frequently listed alongside genioplasty, brow lifts and other facial procedures in surgery-trip threads [8][9][10].

One looksmax.org post described a lip lift as reducing a philtrum from about 2 cm to 1.5 cm, with swelling for the first four to five days and little visible change after eight days; the poster reported paying roughly 450 to 500 dollars at a clinic in Russia [8]. A thread about a commercial subnasal 'philtrum shortening' service asked whether a lift that shortens the philtrum alone is ideal [11]. Another thread asked whether a lip lift is advisable at 15 or whether to wait for full development, and a reply advised waiting until 18 [9].

No studies found specific to philtrum filler. Surgical studies of lip lifts are case series and reviews: Austin's 1986 report of 83 patients [12], a 202-patient retrospective review reporting significantly shorter philtrum length and more visible upper vermilion [13], an 823-patient technique series [14], and the 2014 systematic review described on Wikipedia, which found philtrum length decreased with indirect lip lifts but not with V-Y augmentation [3]. Surgeons report high satisfaction, and no single technique is standard [3].

timeline.event: Paraffin lip injections attempted without success.[6]
Liquid silicone used in lips, later abandoned over safety concerns.[6]
Injectable bovine collagen becomes the benchmark filler.[6]
Early lip lift publications by Fanous, Austin (83 patients, scar hidden under the nose) and Greenwald.[3][12]
Jacono and Quatela report measured increases in upper vermilion height and area after V-Y augmentation [3].
Systematic review finds philtrum length decreased with indirect lip lifts.[3]
Retrospective review of 202 Asian patients reports shorter philtrum length after central lip lift; a narrative review of lip filler technique is published [13][15].
Talei publishes an 823-patient series on a modified upper lip lift with deep-plane release [14].

lore.intro: Philtrum length is a staple of facial-ratio discussion on looksmax.org, where lip lifts are among the more commonly reported soft-tissue surgeries.[8][9]

claims.claim: A lip lift improves several facial ratios at once
claims.believers: One poster reported that removing 0.5 cm of philtrum changed how close-set the eyes looked, improved midface ratio and the chin-to-philtrum ratio, and made thin lips look normal.[8]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports surgeons' high satisfaction with lip lifts but also that no single technique is standard, and describes risks including scarring and lip distortion.[3]

claims.claim: Scars from a lip lift can be hidden
claims.believers: The same poster said BB cream concealed most of the scar and described little visible scarring after two weeks.[8]
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists visible and hypertrophic scarring as lip lift complications, especially when skin is removed at the white roll.[3]

claims.claim: Many people who want a lip lift need only filler or fat
claims.believers: One forum reply suggested that about half of people who think they need a lip lift would be served by fat grafts or filler.[9]
claims.experts: Filler and fat can add volume and definition but do not shorten the philtrum's skin length; Wikipedia describes both options and their durations.[6]

claims.claim: A lip lift is best delayed until growth is complete
claims.believers: A reply to a 15-year-old asking about a lip lift advised waiting until 18.[9]
claims.experts: No published guideline on timing exists.

claims.claim: A shorter philtrum looks younger and more balanced
claims.believers: Forum posters treat philtrum length as a facial ratio and say shortening it improves midface and chin proportions [8].
claims.experts: Austin described upper-lip lengthening as a sign of aging, and surgeons report that a youthful lip has a pronounced cupid's bow [12][3]; no study has tested how viewers rate shorter philtrums.

claims.claim: Lip lifts abroad are a cheap, effective route
claims.believers: One poster reported paying about 450 to 500 dollars at a clinic abroad and was very happy with the result [8]; surgery-trip threads list lip lifts alongside other procedures [10].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists scarring, numbness, asymmetry and smile deformation as possible complications, and says no single technique is standard [3].

claims.claim: A shortened philtrum can change how wide-set the eyes look
claims.believers: The same poster said removing 0.5 cm changed how close-set the eyes looked [8].
claims.experts: No published study has measured perceived eye spacing after a lip lift; a 202-patient review reported improvement in lower-face vertical proportion [13].
